parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.stem:
A polymer, $\mathbf{P}$, can be made from the monomers benzene-1,4-dioyl chloride and benzene-1,3-diamine.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}
parts.text: Draw a section of the polymer chain of $\mathbf{P}$. Your structure should include two repeat units.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text:
Place $\mathbf{one}$ tick in the table to describe polymer $\mathbf{P}$ and its method of polymerisation.

| type of polymer | type of polymerisation |  |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
|  | addition | condensation |
| polyalkene |  |  |
| polyamide |  |  |
| polyester |  |  |

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text: State whether or not polymer $\mathbf{P}$ is biodegradable. Give a reason for your answer.

parts.label: (a)(iv)
parts.text: State a suitable reagent to produce benzene-1,4-dioyl chloride from benzene-1,4-dicarboxylic acid.

parts.label: (a)(v)
(b)(i)
parts.stem: Proteins are natural polymers. A protein is said to have a primary, secondary and tertiary structure.
parts.text: Describe what is meant by each of these terms.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Name the forces or bonds responsible for holding together the primary structure of a protein molecule.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Name the forces or bonds responsible for the stabilisation of the secondary structure of a protein molecule, and identify the groups of atoms within the protein molecule that are held together by these forces or bonds.
